A.explanation: Too small by a factor of $1000$. It results from a prefix error, for example treating $0.50\text{ mg}$ as $0.50 \times 10^{-9}\text{ kg}$ instead of $0.50 \times 10^{-6}\text{ kg}$.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of $10$. It does not equal $mg/q$ with $m = 5.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ kg}$ and $q = 1.0 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}$.

C.explanation: Equals $mg/q = 4.9 \times 10^{-6}\text{ N} / 1.0 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C} = 4.9 \times 10^{6}\text{ N C}^{-1}$ for balanced weight and electric force.

D.explanation: Too large by a factor of $1000$. It results from a prefix error, for example treating $1.0\text{ pC}$ as $1.0 \times 10^{-15}\text{ C}$ instead of $1.0 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}$.

hints: Notice the hair is supported, so the upward electric force $F = EQ$ must balance the downward weight $W = mg$.
Convert the prefixes before substituting: $0.50\text{ mg} = 0.50 \times 10^{-6}\text{ kg}$ and $1.0\text{ pC} = 1.0 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}$.
Use $E = F/q = mg/q$ with $g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$, then check the power of $10$ from $10^{-6}$ divided by $10^{-12}$.
walkthrough: Identify the forces: weight $W = mg$ acts down and electric force $F = EQ$ acts up. Supported means they are equal in magnitude, so $EQ = mg$.
State the rule for field strength: $E = F/q$, so here $E = mg/q$.
Convert mass and charge to SI units: $m = 0.50\text{ mg} = 0.50 \times 10^{-6}\text{ kg} = 5.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ kg}$ and $q = 1.0\text{ pC} = 1.0 \times 10^{-12}\text{ C}$.
Calculate the field strength: $E = 4.9 \times 10^{-6} / 1.0 \times 10^{-12} = 4.9 \times 10^{6}\text{ N C}^{-1}$. The unit $\text{N C}^{-1}$ is correct for $E$.
